create.name: David Treleaven
create.bio:
David Treleaven is a Canadian-born writer and educator who trains meditation and yoga teachers, coaches and other practitioners to offer mindfulness in a way that is safe for people living with trauma. His interest began in 2006 after a difficult experience on a silent meditation retreat, which led him to research how meditation and traumatic stress interact and to write his doctoral dissertation on the subject. He went on to found Trauma-Sensitive Mindfulness, the approach and community he has led since 2016.

His teaching looks at both sides of practice: how sustained inward attention can sometimes bring up overwhelm or dissociation, and how simple adjustments, such as grounding, choice, resourcing and self-compassion, let people stay with practice and draw on its benefits. He offers a two-part online certification course for mindfulness teachers, a free hour-long introductory webinar and a podcast with guests from the meditation world, and he leads talks and workshops for organisations online and in person. His book Trauma-Sensitive Mindfulness (W. W. Norton, 2018) has been translated into ten languages, and a companion workbook for mindfulness teachers followed in 2025.

books.title: Trauma-Sensitive Mindfulness: Practices for Safe and Transformative Healing
books.author: David A. Treleaven
books.description: His 2018 book on why meditation practised without awareness of trauma can sometimes stir up distress, and how teachers can adapt practice around five principles covering attention, arousal, relationship, dissociation and social context. It mixes history, case stories and practical guidance.

courses.title: The Complete Trauma-Sensitive Mindfulness Teacher Training
courses.description: A self-paced, two-part online certification course for mindfulness teachers, coaches and others who guide practice: a five-module foundation followed by a ten-module advanced course. It covers recognising when practice is overwhelming someone and adapting instruction so it stays safe and supportive.

free_resources.title: The Truth About Mindfulness and Trauma
free_resources.description: A free, on-demand training of about an hour for anyone who practises or teaches mindfulness. He explains common pitfalls, how to notice when someone is struggling, and a simple practice for checking safety and steadiness in the moment.

free_resources.title: The Trauma-Sensitive Mindfulness Podcast
free_resources.description: His interview series on meditation, mindfulness and traumatic stress, with guests including Sharon Salzberg, Dan Siegel, Diana Winston, Oren Jay Sofer and Thomas Hübl.
